title: chained `(x << 8) | 5` succeeds on-chain (equal 1-byte operands) but the interpreter aborted — the ACCEPT direction of the same bug

provenance.note: Reconstructed from the per-tier chained tests commit 694c891b added, which pin `(2<<8)|5 === 5`. Kept as a separate entry from the OP_AND case because it is the OPPOSITE verdict direction: a one-sided 'fix' that only makes the interpreter abort more eagerly would pass the OP_AND entry and fail this one.

rationale: `2 << 8` leaves a 1-byte non-minimal [0x00] (OP_LSHIFT preserves length) and the literal 5 is the 1-byte [0x05]; the lengths MATCH so OP_OR succeeds and yields [0x05] = 5, making the spend valid. The buggy interpreters re-minimised `2 << 8` to numeric 0 -> EMPTY array, then hit a length mismatch against [0x05] and rejected a spend the deployed script accepts. Both engines must now accept.
